tools.name: JSONLint
tools.desc: Online JSON validator and formatter with syntax highlighting
pros: Ready to use out of the box, no local install or maintenance
Free tier available, try before you upgrade
cons: Advanced features and higher limits usually require a paid plan
usage:
Step: Open the official site and sign up
Click the red "Visit official site" button to open the JSONLint homepage. Find "Sign Up" and log in with email or Google/GitHub.
Tip:
If the site won’t load, check your connection or try another browser.

Step: Pick the plan that fits you
New users usually get a free trial or free quota. Start with the Free tier before upgrading.
Check:
After sign-up you should see the Dashboard home.

Step: Create your first task / project
Click "New" or "Create New" and follow the guide. Pick the first template to start.
Tip:
Don’t start with a complex request. Test with one simple sentence, e.g. "Summarize this page into 3 points".

Step: Review and save the result
When done, the tool shows the result. Export, copy the link, or save locally.
Check:
If unhappy, click "Regenerate" or tweak the prompt and try again.
tools.detail: JSONLint is an essential tool for developers working with JSON data. It serves as an online JSON validator and formatter, ensuring that your JSON code is syntactically correct and well-formatted. The tool provides syntax highlighting, making it easier to identify and correct errors in your JSON code. Key features include real-time validation, automatic formatting, and support for both standard and non-standard JSON formats. JSONLint is ideal for developers who need to quickly check the validity of their JSON data, debug JSON-related issues, and ensure compliance with JSON standards. While it is a powerful tool for JSON validation, it lacks advanced features like JSON schema validation and may not handle complex JSON structures with nested objects and arrays efficiently.

tools.detail: JSONEditor Online is a versatile and interactive JSON editor designed for developers who need to work with JSON data. It offers syntax highlighting, real-time validation, and formatting, making it easier to manage and manipulate JSON objects and arrays. The editor supports a wide range of JSON features, including nested objects, arrays, and custom data types. Key features include a user-friendly interface, support for large JSON files, and the ability to export and import JSON data. JSONEditor Online is particularly useful for developers who need to collaborate on JSON projects, as it allows multiple users to work on the same JSON document simultaneously. However, it may not be the best choice for complex JSON transformations or when working with extremely large JSON files due to performance limitations.

tools.name: JSONPath
tools.desc: JSON path expression language for querying JSON documents
pros: Free and open source, transparent code, self-hostable for full data control
Supports local / Docker deployment, better data privacy
Free version available, zero cost for personal use
cons: Requires some technical skill to deploy and configure
usage:
Step: Check your environment
This tool runs locally. First make sure your computer meets the basics.
Tip:
Node.js 18 or newer is required.
Check:
Open a terminal and type `node --version`. If you see a version number, your environment is OK.

Step: Download the code to your machine
Open a terminal in a folder you like and run the commands below:
Code:
git clone https://github.com/json-path/JsonPath.git
cd JsonPath
Tip:
New to git? If it says command not found, download it from https://git-scm.com.

Step: Install dependencies
The project needs some extra building blocks to run.
Code:
npm install
Tip:
If a command errors, it is usually a network issue. Python users can try a mirror.

Step: Fill in the API Key / account config
Many AI tools need a model connection. Find the config item in the README and fill it in.
Code:
# Example: replace xxx with your real Key
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-xxx"
Tip:
Do not screenshot your Key in public groups. Get a free/cheap Key (e.g. GLM-4, DeepSeek) to practice.

Step: Start and run your first task
Run the example command from the project and watch the terminal output.
Code:
npm run example
Check:
If the program prints results (no red Error text), you have it working.

Step: Troubleshooting
Failing the first local deploy is normal. Common issues:
1. Dependency version mismatch → use the Python/Node version the repo recommends;
2. Key not working → check your environment variables;
3. Cannot reach the model API → switch mirror or provider.
Tip:
See more examples in "Related tutorials" below, or click "Visit official site".
tools.detail: JSONPath is a powerful tool for querying JSON documents using a path expression language. It allows developers to extract specific data from JSON objects and arrays, making it easier to manipulate and process JSON data. Key features include support for a wide range of JSON query operations, such as filtering, mapping, and transforming JSON data. JSONPath is particularly useful for developers who need to perform complex data extraction and manipulation tasks on JSON documents. It is widely used in various programming languages and frameworks, making it a versatile tool for JSON data processing. However, JSONPath may have a steep learning curve for beginners, and it may not be suitable for all types of JSON data due to its specific query capabilities.
